hadith:
Virtues of the Night of Qadr - Narrated Abu Huraira:

The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Whoever fasted the month of Ramadan out of sincere Faith (i.e. belief) and hoping for a reward from Allah, then all his past sins will be forgiven, and whoever stood for the prayers in the night of Qadr out of sincere Faith and hoping for a reward from Allah, then all his previous sins will be forgiven ."
message: On the Day of Judgment, we will be held accountable for our deeds and knowledge, as mentioned in Surah An-Naml, reminding us to live with conscious awareness of Allah's watching. Yet Allah, The Glorious (Al Maajid), offers us countless opportunities for forgiveness in this life—particularly during Ramadan and the Night of Qadr, when sincere fasting and night prayers can erase our past sins. Let this be a motivation to seek Allah's mercy with genuine faith while we still have time.
name:
Al Maajid - الْمَاجِدُ - The Glorious

The name Al Maajid emphasizes the glory and majesty of Allah. It highlights His honor and the reverence He commands in the hearts of believers. The origin of this name comes from the Arabic root related to honor and magnificence, reflecting the Islamic belief in Allah's supremacy and grandeur in all aspects of existence.
verse:
An-Naml - The Ant - 27:84-85

When they ˹finally˺ come before their Lord, He will ask ˹them˺, “Did you deny My revelations without ˹even˺ comprehending them? Or what ˹exactly˺ did you do?”

And the decree ˹of torment˺ will be justified against them for their wrongdoing, leaving them speechless.
